newsitem.title: USA: Hot dogs recalled because of faulty label.
newsitem.headline: Hot dogs recalled because of faulty label.

text.p: A Detroit meat processor is voluntarily recalling about 80,000 pounds (36,000 kg) of hot dogs because they may contain milk protein though it is not listed as an ingredient on the label, the U.S. Agriculture Department said on Wednesday
Milk protein can cause serious reactions in people allergic to milk products.

Hygrade Food Products is recalling all 14-ounce packages of "Ball Park Fat Free Franks, Smoke Flavoring Added," with the bar code number 545393 and a sell by code beginning with "Sep03A" or "Sep03C." The hot dogs were distributed nationwide except for New England.

The Agriculture Department said it learned about the problem from a consumer who reported an allergic reaction by her son. Laboratory tests found milk protein in the hot dogs though it was not listed as an ingredient. Hygrade said milk protein was inadvertently included in the product, USDA said.
